keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.

keywords.name: LLM agents
keywords.about: Agents get verifiable task synthesis, procedural memory and memory-arranged planning scaffolds for long-horizon work.

keywords.name: Vision-language models
keywords.about: Vision-language models are probed for hallucination signals, out-of-distribution detection and scientific figure understanding.

keywords.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
keywords.about: Retrieval bottlenecks, geo-distributed serving and configuration benchmarks diagnose evidence-grounded generation and question answering.

keywords.name: EEG

keywords.name: Cross-attention
keywords.about: Cross-attention blocks fuse audio-text, drug-target and point-cloud features across modalities.

keywords.name: Latent world models

keywords.name: Code generation
keywords.about: LLMs generate RTL and general code, helped by multi-teacher distillation and diffusion decomposition.

keywords.name: Long-horizon agents

keywords.name: Long-tailed learning

keywords.name: 3D Gaussian splatting

keywords.name: ASR

themes.name: Reliability-grounded multimodal clinical AI
themes.summary: The papers develop clinical AI systems that integrate speech, text, imaging, and physiological signals for assessment and decision support. They emphasize reliability, evidence grounding, interpretability, and deployment constraints, differing in modalities and tasks such as depression screening, radiology structuring, and medical image segmentation.

themes.name: Runtime safety and control for AI agents
themes.summary: These papers build frameworks, benchmarks, and defenses for securing LLM agents as they act across multi-step, stateful workflows. They differ in threat model and intervention point: some gate execution, memory, or tool calls at runtime, others red-team or measure agent sabotage, manipulation, and prompt-injection behavior, and others benchmark silent tool errors and recovery in long-horizon tasks.

themes.name: Memory and harness evolution for long-horizon agents
themes.summary: The papers study how LLM and embodied agents store, retrieve, and evolve reusable knowledge over long horizons, using external memories, procedural memories, latent beliefs, codified retrieval, and self-evolving harnesses or skill libraries. They differ in whether memory is written through test-time training, structured as skills and graphs, maintained as multi-hypothesis state, or replaced by harness and tool evolution. Several also benchmark whether such memory and context compaction actually help later tasks.

themes.name: Latent world models for embodied planning
themes.summary: These papers learn latent or predictive world models from observations, video, and actions to forecast future states or representations for planning, control, manipulation, and navigation. They differ in whether they predict pixels, latent changes, values, occupancy, or terminal maps, and in their use of JEPA-style architectures, language or latent actions, multi-view inputs, object-structured slots, configurable perception, and quantum priors.

themes.name: Benchmarking and evaluating LLM and VLM capabilities
themes.summary: These papers introduce benchmarks and evaluation frameworks that probe the capabilities of large language models and vision-language models across planning, tool use, scientific figures, multilingual web agents, values, and reasoning. They differ in modality and task focus, and in whether they contribute new datasets, diagnostic audits of existing benchmarks, or adaptive sampling methods for efficient comparison.

themes.name: Multi-agent LLM collaboration and credit assignment
themes.summary: The papers examine multi-agent LLM systems: when collaboration beats single agents, how to evaluate intermediate reasoning and hallucination, and how to design or train agent teams. They differ in domain, from clinical and financial review to argument graphs, simulation, robotics, and video editing, and in method, from empirical comparisons to verification frameworks and credit-assignment algorithms.

themes.name: Diffusion and flow matching for controllable generation
themes.summary: The papers develop diffusion- and flow-matching-based generative frameworks for controllable synthesis and editing across images, video, 3D scenes, code, and scientific design tasks. They differ in the modality addressed, the controllability mechanism used (such as attention anchoring, trajectory primitives, or compositional scores), and whether they contribute methods, theory, or benchmarks.

themes.name: Sparsity, pruning, and speculative decoding for efficient inference
themes.summary: Papers in this theme reduce LLM serving and deployment costs by sparsifying or sharing experts, pruning experts and depth, compressing attention and KV caches, quantizing weights, and accelerating decoding with speculative or multi-token prediction. They differ in whether they target Mixture-of-Experts banks, dense attention or layer structure, quantization calibration, or draft-verify decoding, and in their use of training-free calibration versus learned components.

themes.name: Mechanistic interpretability of transformer internal representations
themes.summary: The papers probe how transformer representations, circuits, and layer states encode and support behavior, using methods such as linear probing, sparse dictionaries, activation patching, and Jacobian lenses. They differ in whether they analyze inference trajectories, causal component importance, steering control, confidence readouts, or cross-model representation alignment. Together they aim to connect internal mechanisms to measurable model behavior.

themes.name: Retrieval-augmented generation and evidence grounding
themes.summary: The papers develop retrieval-augmented systems that improve how evidence is retrieved, ranked, and grounded for question answering and generation. They span speech, visual, clinical, scholarly, and transactional settings, and differ in retrieval architecture, reranking, and evaluation design. Several contributions target benchmarks, abstention, and citation-level grounding.

themes.name: VLA and Embodied VLM Robotic Manipulation
themes.summary: Papers in this theme develop and evaluate embodied vision-language and vision-language-action agents for robot manipulation, spanning spatial grounding, tactile and contact reasoning, planning, and robustness. They differ in whether they propose training methods, recovery and failure-attribution mechanisms, or diagnostic benchmarks and cross-model evaluations.

themes.name: Privacy, unlearning, and watermarking in generative models
themes.summary: These papers examine how generative language, speech, and diffusion models expose or retain sensitive information, and propose techniques to control that exposure. Methods include calibrated target-band unlearning, orthogonal boundary unlearning, differential-privacy accounting and auditing, watermark embedding and attacks on watermarks, memorization detection, and model fingerprinting. They differ in whether they remove information from trained models, formally bound disclosure during release or inference, or embed and detect identifying signals in generated output.

highlights.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
highlights.authors: Qiayuan Liao, Yiyang Shao, Junfeng Long et al.
highlights.theme: Latent world models for embodied planning
highlights.why: Reports a >1000x compute reduction for humanoid whole-body control using a differentiable world model, a major practical advance in embodied learning.
highlights.key_result: In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs, reduces GPU-hours by more than 1000 , and fails on only 25 of 129514 benchmark motions versus 179 for the baseline; after 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures.

It reduces GPU-hours by more than 1000 and fails on only 25 of 129514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures.

highlights.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
highlights.authors: Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Yue Zhao, Armin W. Thomas et al.
highlights.why: Shows strong text-to-image generation without language pretraining, challenging a common assumption and offering large compute savings.
highlights.key_result: Particularly, -0.52B achieves 48.0 gFD, outperforming LlamaGen-XL/8 (FLAN-T5-XL 1.22B + 0.90B image generator; 63.3 gFD) using 18.2 less total pretraining compute. -1.6B achieves 35.3 gFD, outperforming JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (Qwen3-1.7B + 1.10B image generator; 41.0 gFD) using 275 less total pretraining compute.

highlights.title: A general-purpose System One decision model for clinical records
highlights.authors: Andrew Zhang, Trinh T.L. Vuong, Sophia J. Wagner et al.
highlights.why: Releases a 4B clinical decision model with strong population-scale performance, potentially useful for deployments though trained on proprietary data.
highlights.key_result: On 963,408 held-out patients, CS1-4B outperformed open decision models up to 27 billion parameters on 13 of 14 tasks scored independently of its training teacher. highlights.title: On the Limits of Scale: Inverse Scaling in Vision-Language Models
highlights.authors: Rohit Saxena, Alessandro Suglia, Marek Rei et al.
highlights.theme: Benchmarking and evaluating LLM and VLM capabilities
highlights.why: Documents systematic inverse scaling in vision-language models at the subtask level, an important nuance to scaling laws with broad evaluation evidence.
highlights.key_result: We evaluate 19 models across 4 families and eight benchmarks. Through per-question pairwise analysis, we identify 375 cases in which smaller models outperform larger ones, with 13 subtask types showing this pattern across multiple families.

highlights.title: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence in LLM Agents
highlights.authors: Ruhan Wang, Kishan Panaganti, Dongruo Zhou
highlights.theme: Memory and harness evolution for long-horizon agents
highlights.why: Shows that abstraction-based experience memory can hurt agents via error reproduction, a counterintuitive result important for memory design.
highlights.key_result: Across different benchmarks and backbones, Anti-Persistence achieved higher overall held-out success and the lowest average LLM-call cost among the evaluated memory designs: averaged equally across settings it reached 59.9%, compared with 53.5% for trajectory memory, 49.0% for abstraction memory, and 49.3% for joint memory.
evidence: Across different benchmarks and backbones, Anti-Persistence achieves higher overall held-out success and the lowest average LLM-call cost among the evaluated memory designs.
Averaged equally across settings, it reached 59.9%, compared with 53.5% for trajectory memory, 49.0% for abstraction memory, and 49.3% for joint memory.
Across the nine settings, anti-persistence achieved the lowest mean LLM-call cost among the four memory configurations, alongside the highest mean success ( fig:cost-summary).

highlights.title: Local Allow, Global Deny: Why Per-Action Authorization Does Not Compose in LLM Agents
highlights.authors: Anmol Pandey, Aditya Jain, Liang Chen et al.
highlights.theme: Runtime safety and control for AI agents
highlights.why: Provides a formal impossibility result showing per-action authorization cannot compose into global safety, a fundamental and actionable negative result.
highlights.key_result: The paper's central result is an impossibility: relational purpose violations form a 2-safety hyperproperty with no per-trace locus of blame, so a per-action monitor that never raises a false alarm detects none of them, independent of the underlying model or decision procedure; they become visible only under cross-execution monitoring, which none of the six guardrails surveyed implements. Empirically, across nine LLM judges the per-action view approves the synthesized witness almost without exception, yet the same models flag it when shown the two executions together.
evidence: Our central result is an impossibility: relational purpose violations form a 2-safety hyperproperty with no per-trace locus of blame, so a per-action monitor that never raises a false alarm detects none of them, independent of the underlying model or decision procedure; they become visible only under cross-execution monitoring, which none of the six guardrails we survey implements.

The empirical signature is sharp: across nine LLM judges the per-action view approves the synthesized witness almost without exception, blocking it at a rate comparable to a benign control, yet the same models flag it when shown the two executions together.

highlights.title: When Does Experience Memory Help Closed-Loop LLM Driving Agents? A Controlled Evaluation with Resampled Warmup Pools, Token-Matched Fillers, and Audited Baselines
highlights.theme: Memory and harness evolution for long-horizon agents
highlights.why: Rigorously controlled evaluation finds memory gains depend on warmup draws and token effects, challenging prior claims in closed-loop driving agents.
highlights.key_result: On this testbed, memory effects were dominated by pool and prompt composition rather than by what the memory stored, and even our own strongest claim survived only until the evaluation's resampling control reached it. highlights.title: Forty Questions: Identifying a Language Model from One-Word Answers
highlights.theme: Privacy, unlearning, and watermarking in generative models
highlights.why: Demonstrates that one-word answers can identify a model among 94 with 92.5% accuracy, a surprisingly simple and effective fingerprinting method.
highlights.key_result: A model behind an API can be identified from its one-word answers to everyday questions such as ``Name a sound'' or ``Name a poet''. On a panel of 94 models, 40 answers identify the exact model 92.5% of the time, against 1.1% by chance.

On a panel of 94 models, 40 answers identify the exact model 92.5% of the time, against 1.1% by chance.

news.title: Franchisee reconciles cash in 94% less time with ChatGPT Work
news.summary: A New Mexico franchisee of three co-branded Schlotzsky's and Cinnabon restaurants used ChatGPT Work to cut menu repricing analysis from 5 days to 1–2 hours (a 95% reduction) and monthly cash reconciliation time by 94%, plus 4 hours saved per payroll run. The item states the optimized labor workflow could free up a maximum of $100K in annual cash flow.

news.title: Terminal X matches senior investor judgment 88.6% with GPT-6.1
news.summary: Terminal X's Eval Agent, which grades agent output against a 54-criterion rubric, caught about 25% more recommendations straying from a fund's mandate on GPT-6.1 Sol versus the next-best model, with +220bps higher agreement with human reviewers and 30% lower cost per query. One private equity customer reported $2.4 million in annualized savings from automated due diligence and investment memo workflows.

news.title: Spain-Based Startups Advance Regional Innovation With Barcelona Supercomputing Center
news.summary: The Barcelona Supercomputing Center's AI Factory Accelerator Programme is now in full operation after a pilot, with some services accessible through the NVIDIA Inception portal; the BSC AI Factory has delivered more than 800 services since its April 2025 launch. Three Inception members were named AI Champions, including Qatium, whose water-network platform is used by more than 250 utilities in 16 countries.

news.title: NVIDIA Cosmos3-H-Dreams: Bringing Clinical Surgery to Life Through Generative Simulation
news.summary: NVIDIA introduced Cosmos3-H-Dreams, a real-time generative surgical simulator built on the 16-billion-parameter Cosmos3-H-Embodied-Nano and trained on clinical cholecystectomy recordings from the CMR Surgical Versius platform, running interactively on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU. It uses 28 action dimensions and 832 x 480 video with actions aligned at 10 Hz, with a teacher adapted on 24 future frames before extending to 72 frames.

news.title: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
news.summary: Hugging Face released FairStress, a benchmark with 300 realistic two-candidate decision scenarios across 29 domains, available for download and built into Olmo-eval, measuring whether models change decisions equally under persuasive adversarial prefixes. Across Olmo, Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Claude and the GPT family, the authors report the same arguments make models more or less likely to switch decisions depending on which demographic group the argument favors.

news.title: ALTK-Evolve: How learned memory tops the τ²-bench leaderboard on customer service tasks without a frontier model
news.summary: ALTK-Evolve distills behavioral guidelines from an agent's training-task trajectories using GPT-4.1 and appends them to the system prompt, reaching 67.5% Pass^4 on τ²-bench retail with the stock ReAct scaffold and no weight updates, above every retail entry in the October 12, 2026 leaderboard snapshot. The authors compare no-guideline, high-support (31 retail / 14 airline guidelines) and lossless (292 / 101) configurations.

news.title: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
news.summary: i14 and AWS trained and served the Laplace 3B linear-attention model (Gated Linear Attention, Muon optimizer) on AWS Trainium2 using TorchNeuron Native, with a recurrent state fixed at 29.5 MB per sequence independent of context length. On one trn2.48xlarge instance it trained at about 120,000 tokens per second and served 11,544 output tokens per second across 1,280 concurrent sequences, with Muon communication changes cutting per-rank traffic 24 times and raising throughput 1.63 times.

news.title: Work management context for AI agents with Smartsheet MCP on AWS
news.summary: Smartsheet launched a generally available Model Context Protocol Server that lets AI assistants read, write and manage Smartsheet data via more than 40 tools, connected to Amazon Quick and Kiro as MCP clients. The post describes a sprint-management example where Kiro updates a row's status on commit.

news.title: From data to decisions: Conversational supply chain intelligence with Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: The post describes a pattern using Amazon Quick over Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to expose enterprise MCP servers as a tool layer for supply chain queries, replacing a manual flow of 45–60 minutes across five systems. In the walkthrough, a disruption assessment (DISR-002) returns $750K at risk, 23 orders and three days of supply.

news.title: Fine-tuning GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
news.summary: AWS fine-tuned GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on SageMaker HyperPod using LoRA, with SFT followed by GRPO; the base model reasoned in the requested target language only 22% of the time (English 100%, French 0%, German 10%, Spanish 0%, Italian 0%) on a 50-example test. Training used HuggingFaceH4/Multilingual-Thinking with roughly 949 training and 50 validation examples, plus a Qwen2.5-7B control experiment; the authors conclude SFT does most of the work and GRPO refines when headroom exists.

highlights.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
highlights.authors: Qiayuan Liao, Yiyang Shao, Junfeng Long et al.
highlights.theme: Latent world models for embodied planning
highlights.why: 报告了使用可微世界模型实现人形全身控制的计算量减少 >1000x，这是具身学习中的重大实际进展。
highlights.key_result: 在单个 GPU 上用 3 小时，SuperMimic 超越了训练 7 天、使用 128 个 GPU 的最先进运动跟踪基线所达到的回报，将 GPU 小时数减少了 1000 以上，并且在 129514 个基准运动中仅失败 25 个，而基线失败 179 个；在两个 GPU 上运行 9.8 小时后，SuperMimic 实现零失败。
evidence: In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs.
It reduces GPU-hours by more than 1000 and fails on only 25 of 129514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures.

highlights.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
highlights.authors: Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Yue Zhao, Armin W. Thomas et al.
highlights.why: 展示了无需语言预训练的强文本到图像生成能力，挑战了常见假设，并带来大量计算节省。
highlights.key_result: 具体而言，-0.52B 达到 48.0 gFD，超越 LlamaGen-XL/8（FLAN-T5-XL 1.22B + 0.90B 图像生成器；63.3 gFD），其使用的总预训练计算量少 18.2。 -1.6B 达到 35.3 gFD，超越 JiT-T2I-XXL/8++（Qwen3-1.7B + 1.10B 图像生成器；41.0 gFD），其使用的总预训练计算量少 275。
evidence: Particularly, -0.52B achieves 48.0 gFD, outperforming LlamaGen-XL/8 (FLAN-T5-XL 1.22B + 0.90B image generator; 63.3 gFD) using 18.2 less total pretraining compute. -1.6B achieves 35.3 gFD, outperforming JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (Qwen3-1.7B + 1.10B image generator; 41.0 gFD) using 275 less total pretraining compute.

highlights.title: A general-purpose System One decision model for clinical records
highlights.authors: Andrew Zhang, Trinh T.L. Vuong, Sophia J. Wagner et al.
highlights.why: 发布了一个 4B 临床决策模型，具有强大的人群规模性能，尽管基于专有数据训练，但仍可能对部署有用。
highlights.key_result: 在 963,408 名留出患者上，CS1-4B 在 14 项任务中的 13 项上优于参数量高达 27 billion 的开源决策模型，且这些任务独立于其训练教师模型评分。在 21 个外部数据集上，其综合性能接近所测试的最强 27 billion 参数模型，且在匹配工作负载下推理速度快 6.4 倍。
evidence: On 963,408 held-out patients, CS1-4B outperformed open decision models up to 27 billion parameters on 13 of 14 tasks scored independently of its training teacher. Across 21 external data sets, its aggregate performance approached that of the strongest tested 27-billion-parameter model, with 6.4-fold faster inference in a matched workload.

highlights.title: On the Limits of Scale: Inverse Scaling in Vision-Language Models
highlights.authors: Rohit Saxena, Alessandro Suglia, Marek Rei et al.
highlights.theme: Benchmarking and evaluating LLM and VLM capabilities
highlights.why: 记录了视觉语言模型在子任务层面上的系统性逆缩放现象，这是对缩放定律的重要细微补充，并具有广泛的评估证据。
highlights.key_result: 我们评估了 4 个家族中的 19 个模型以及八个基准。通过逐问题的 pairwise 分析，我们识别出 375 个较小模型优于较大模型的案例，其中 13 个子任务类型在多个家族中均表现出这一模式。
evidence: We evaluate 19 models across 4 families and eight benchmarks. Through per-question pairwise analysis, we identify 375 cases in which smaller models outperform larger ones, with 13 subtask types showing this pattern across multiple families.

highlights.title: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence in LLM Agents
highlights.authors: Ruhan Wang, Kishan Panaganti, Dongruo Zhou
highlights.theme: Memory and harness evolution for long-horizon agents
highlights.why: 表明基于抽象的经验记忆可能通过错误复制损害智能体，这一反直觉的结果对记忆设计很重要。
highlights.key_result: 在不同基准和骨干网络上，Anti-Persistence 在评估的记忆设计中实现了更高的整体留出成功率以及最低的平均 LLM 调用成本：在各设置等权平均下，它达到 59.9%，而轨迹记忆为 53.5%，抽象记忆为 49.0%，联合记忆为 49.3%。
evidence: Across different benchmarks and backbones, Anti-Persistence achieves higher overall held-out success and the lowest average LLM-call cost among the evaluated memory designs.
Averaged equally across settings, it reached 59.9%, compared with 53.5% for trajectory memory, 49.0% for abstraction memory, and 49.3% for joint memory.
Across the nine settings, anti-persistence achieved the lowest mean LLM-call cost among the four memory configurations, alongside the highest mean success ( fig:cost-summary).

highlights.title: Local Allow, Global Deny: Why Per-Action Authorization Does Not Compose in LLM Agents
highlights.authors: Anmol Pandey, Aditya Jain, Liang Chen et al.
highlights.theme: Runtime safety and control for AI agents
highlights.why: 提供了一个形式化的不可能性结果，表明逐动作授权无法组合成全局安全，这是一个根本且可操作的负面结果。
highlights.key_result: 本文的核心结果是一个不可能性：关系目的违规形成了一种 2-safety 超性质，没有逐轨迹的归责点，因此从不误报的逐动作监控器无法检测到其中任何一个，这与底层模型或决策程序无关；它们仅在跨执行监控下才可见，而所调查的六个护栏均未实现跨执行监控。实证上，在九个 LLM 评判器中，逐动作视图几乎无一例外地批准了合成的见证，但当同时展示两次执行时，相同的模型却会标记它。
evidence: Our central result is an impossibility: relational purpose violations form a 2-safety hyperproperty with no per-trace locus of blame, so a per-action monitor that never raises a false alarm detects none of them, independent of the underlying model or decision procedure; they become visible only under cross-execution monitoring, which none of the six guardrails we survey implements.

The empirical signature is sharp: across nine LLM judges the per-action view approves the synthesized witness almost without exception, blocking it at a rate comparable to a benign control, yet the same models flag it when shown the two executions together.

highlights.title: When Does Experience Memory Help Closed-Loop LLM Driving Agents? A Controlled Evaluation with Resampled Warmup Pools, Token-Matched Fillers, and Audited Baselines
highlights.theme: Memory and harness evolution for long-horizon agents
highlights.why: 严格控制的评估发现记忆增益取决于预热抽取和 token 效应，挑战了之前关于闭环驾驶智能体的主张。
highlights.key_result: 在此测试平台上，记忆效应主要由提示池和提示组合主导，而非记忆存储的内容，甚至我们自己最强的主张也仅在评估的重采样控制触及之前得以维持。所报告的提示池是两个检索记忆在十个提示池中的最佳结果，它们仅在十个提示池中的一个上击败 No-Memory（符号检验 \(p\!=\!0.011\)），且具有负的池平均效应；甚至规则手册在五个提示池上表现出的表观池免疫性（从 \(0.97\) 到 \(0.98\)）在五次新抽取中崩溃至 \(0.03\) 到 \(0.98\)。
evidence: On this testbed, memory effects were dominated by pool and prompt composition rather than by what the memory stored, and even our own strongest claim survived only until the evaluation's resampling control reached it.

The reported pool is the best of ten for both retrieval memories, which beat No-Memory in only one pool of ten (sign test \(p\!=\!0.011\)) and have a negative pool-averaged effect, and even the rulebook's apparent pool-immunity (\(0.97\) to \(0.98\) on five pools) collapsed to \(0.03\) to \(0.98\) on five fresh draws.

highlights.title: Forty Questions: Identifying a Language Model from One-Word Answers
highlights.theme: Privacy, unlearning, and watermarking in generative models
highlights.why: 证明了单字回答可以在 94 个模型中识别出模型，准确率达 92.5%，这是一种出奇简单且有效的指纹识别方法。
highlights.key_result: 一个隐藏在 API 后面的模型可以通过其对日常问题（如“说出一种声音”或“说出一位诗人”）的单字回答被识别出来。在包含 94 个模型的面板上，40 个回答在 92.5% 的情况下能识别出确切模型，而随机猜测仅为 1.1%。
evidence: A model behind an API can be identified from its one-word answers to everyday questions such as ``Name a sound'' or ``Name a poet''. A model's profile records how often it gives each answer to each question. We attribute new answers to the model most likely to have given them. On a panel of 94 models, 40 answers identify the exact model 92.5% of the time, against 1.1% by chance.

news.title: Franchisee reconciles cash in 94% less time with ChatGPT Work
news.summary: 新墨西哥州一家拥有三家 Schlotzsky's 和 Cinnabon 联合品牌餐厅的特许经营商使用 ChatGPT Work，将菜单重新定价分析时间从 5 天缩短至 1–2 小时（减少 95%），并将月度现金对账时间缩短 94%，此外每次薪资运行节省 4 小时。该项目指出，优化后的劳动力工作流程每年最多可释放 $100K 现金流。

news.title: Terminal X matches senior investor judgment 88.6% with GPT-6.1
news.summary: Terminal X 的 Eval Agent 根据 54 项标准评分标准对智能体输出进行评分，在 GPT-6.1 Sol 上捕获了比次优模型多约 25% 偏离基金授权的建议，与人工审核员的一致率高出 +220bps，每次查询成本低 30%。一位私募股权客户报告称，通过自动化尽职调查和投资备忘录工作流程，每年节省 $2.4 million。

news.title: Spain-Based Startups Advance Regional Innovation With Barcelona Supercomputing Center
news.summary: The Barcelona Supercomputing Center's AI Factory Accelerator Programme is now in full operation after a pilot, with some services accessible through the NVIDIA Inception portal; the BSC AI Factory has delivered more than 800 services since its April 2025 launch. Three Inception members were named AI Champions, including Qatium, whose water-network platform is used by more than 250 utilities in 16 countries.

news.title: NVIDIA Cosmos3-H-Dreams: Bringing Clinical Surgery to Life Through Generative Simulation
news.summary: NVIDIA 推出了 Cosmos3-H-Dreams，一个实时生成式手术模拟器，基于 16 billion 参数的 Cosmos3-H-Embodied-Nano 构建，并在 CMR Surgical Versius 平台的临床胆囊切除术录像上训练，可在单个 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU 上交互运行。它使用 28 个动作维度和 832 x 480 视频，动作以 10 Hz 对齐，教师模型在扩展到 72 帧之前在 24 个未来帧上进行了适配。

news.title: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
news.summary: Hugging Face 发布了 FairStress，一个包含 300 个真实双候选人决策场景的基准，涵盖 29 个领域，可供下载并已集成到 Olmo-eval 中，测量模型在具有说服力的对抗性前缀下是否平等地改变决策。在 Olmo、Llama、Qwen、Gemma、Claude 和 GPT 系列模型中，作者报告称，相同的论点会使模型根据论点所偏向的人口群体更可能或更不可能改变决策。

news.title: ALTK-Evolve: How learned memory tops the τ²-bench leaderboard on customer service tasks without a frontier model
news.summary: ALTK-Evolve distills behavioral guidelines from an agent's training-task trajectories using GPT-4.1 and appends them to the system prompt, reaching 67.5% Pass^4 on τ²-bench retail with the stock ReAct scaffold and no weight updates, above every retail entry in the October 12, 2026 leaderboard snapshot. The authors compare no-guideline, high-support (31 retail / 14 airline guidelines) and lossless (292 / 101) configurations.

news.title: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
news.summary: i14 和 AWS 在 AWS Trainium2 上使用 TorchNeuron Native 训练并服务了 Laplace 3B 线性注意力模型（门控线性注意力，Muon 优化器），其递归状态固定为每条序列 29.5 MB，与上下文长度无关。在一台 trn2.48xlarge 实例上，它训练速度约为每秒 120,000 个 token，在 1,280 条并发序列上每秒提供 11,544 个输出 token，Muon 通信更改使每 rank 流量减少 24 倍，吞吐量提高 1.63 倍。

news.title: Work management context for AI agents with Smartsheet MCP on AWS
news.summary: Smartsheet 推出了一个正式可用的 Model Context Protocol Server，允许 AI 助手通过超过 40 个工具读取、写入和管理 Smartsheet 数据，并与作为 MCP 客户端的 Amazon Quick 和 Kiro 连接。该帖子描述了一个冲刺管理示例，其中 Kiro 在提交时更新某一行的状态。

news.title: From data to decisions: Conversational supply chain intelligence with Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: 这篇文章描述了一种模式，使用 Amazon Quick 基于 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 将企业 MCP 服务器暴露为用于供应链查询的工具层，取代了跨五个系统的 45–60 分钟手动流程。在演示中，一次中断评估（DISR-002）返回 $750K 风险敞口、23 个订单和三天的供应量。

news.title: Fine-tuning GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
news.summary: AWS 在 SageMaker HyperPod 上使用 LoRA 对 GPT-OSS-20B 进行多语言推理微调，先进行 SFT 再进行 GRPO；基础模型在 50 个示例的测试中，仅在 22% 的情况下以请求的目标语言进行推理（英语 100%，法语 0%，德语 10%，西班牙语 0%，意大利语 0%）。训练使用了 HuggingFaceH4/Multilingual-Thinking 数据集，约 949 个训练示例和 50 个验证示例，另外还有一个 Qwen2.5-7B 对照实验；作者得出结论，SFT 完成了大部分工作，而 GRPO 在有提升空间时进行细化。
